hindi: माना $ABCD$ एक चतुष्फलक है जिसमें $AB=2$, $AC=3$, $AD=4$ तथा प्रत्येक कोण $\angle BAC$, $\angle CAD$ तथा $\angle DAB$, $60^\circ$ के बराबर है। माना $\overrightarrow{u}=\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{v}=\overrightarrow{AC}$ तथा $\overrightarrow{w}=\overrightarrow{AD}$ है। तब
solution_full: For any four vectors, $(\overrightarrow{a}\times\overrightarrow{b})\cdot(\overrightarrow{c}\times\overrightarrow{d})=\begin{vmatrix}\overrightarrow{a}\cdot\overrightarrow{c}&\overrightarrow{a}\cdot\overrightarrow{d}\\\overrightarrow{b}\cdot\overrightarrow{c}&\overrightarrow{b}\cdot\overrightarrow{d}\end{vmatrix}$, so no coordinates are needed.

Dot products from the data: $\overrightarrow{u}\cdot\overrightarrow{v}=2\cdot3\cos60^\circ=3$, $\overrightarrow{v}\cdot\overrightarrow{w}=3\cdot4\cos60^\circ=6$, $\overrightarrow{w}\cdot\overrightarrow{u}=4\cdot2\cos60^\circ=4$, and $|\overrightarrow{u}|^2=4$, $|\overrightarrow{v}|^2=9$, $|\overrightarrow{w}|^2=16$.

Check with coordinates: $\overrightarrow{u}=(2,0,0)$, $\overrightarrow{v}=\left(\dfrac32,\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2},0\right)$, $\overrightarrow{w}=\left(2,\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3},\dfrac{4\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}\right)$ have the same lengths and angles and give the same sum $-54$.
originality_note: New: a tetrahedron given only by its edge lengths and angles at one vertex, with a cyclic sum of dot products of face-normal vectors evaluated through the four-vector identity without coordinates (way 5). Closest known: evaluating (a x b).(c x d) for given vectors, or the dihedral angle of a regular tetrahedron. Different because: three cyclic terms built on a non-regular corner must each be reduced to Gram data.

concept_use.Scalar and vector products of four vecto: Each term (a x b).(c x d) is replaced by (a.c)(b.d)-(a.d)(b.c), so the sum is computed from the dot products 3, 6, 4 and the squared lengths.

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line and plane is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy and numpy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan; the options have one form and exactly one is correct. The three angles at A and the three edge lengths fix all dot products; the expression is displayed on its own line so that it has one reading. Changed: No change.
key_step: Applying the identity (a x b).(c x d) = (a.c)(b.d) - (a.d)(b.c) to three cyclic terms.
justification: One standard identity applied three times with dot products from angles; routine multi-step, no insight. Like the vector-algebra chain of 2026-P2-Q1 (L2), below the Gram-data volume question 2021-P1-Q19 (L3).
